# odyssey-078 (Odyssey 16.112–212) — review, pass 1 (translation)

Reviewer: strongest model, adversarial. Read in full: `conventions.md` (all 1,821 lines, house table to row 1815 and the Notes/Glossary sections), `runbook.md`, `packet.md`, `new-renderings.md`, `units.json` (65 units). Shipped English consulted only from the repository's own `odyssey-0NN.json` files (for repeat checks and house wording); no modern translation was consulted. `gloss.json` not read (pass 2). No scansion flags in the packet, so no hand-scan was due. Edits were made to `units.json` by script; `t`, `ln`, `p`, `mark`, `v`, `title`, `titleEn`, `part` and `about` are byte-identical to the draft (checked after writing), and the `l` line counts still match `t`.

## What was checked and found sound

- **Tiling**: the `t` fields, joined, reproduce the packet's 101 lines exactly; every `ln` is the line the unit starts on; every Murray ¶ (112, 135, 146, 154, 167, 172, 181, 186, 190, 194, 201) carries `p` and nothing else does.
- **Speech marks**: eight speeches, each with `mark` and “ on its first unit in both layers and ” on its last unit in both layers: Telemachus 113–134 (units 1–15), Eumaeus 136–145 (17–21), Telemachus 147–153 (23–27), Athena 167–171 (37–39), Telemachus 181–185 (46–48), Odysseus 187–189 (50–52), Telemachus 194–200 (56–59), Odysseus 202–212 (61–64). Nothing is open at either seam: odyssey-077's last unit (16.111) ends with ” in both layers and closes Odysseus' speech, and 078's last unit closes his reply, which is the part end.
- **Cross-references in notes**: every "line N" / "lines N–M" / "middle of line N" / "two lines later" / "three times in this part" claim was checked against the packet (lines 112, 127, 133, 139–141, 140, 142, 145, 155, 166, 167, 170, 181, 183, 191, 198, 200; and 1.245–248 against odyssey-003, where the unit stands at 1.245). All true.
- **Repeats**: the units for 112, 113, 126, 135, 146, 186, 201 match their published English exactly. Line-level repeats (116, 122–125, 129, 158, 167, 180) reuse the published wording. The failures are listed below.
- **Grammatical labels**: every label in every note was checked against the form and the line. Four were wrong or misleading (unit 21 twice, unit 24, unit 26) and are fixed below; the rest are true.
- **Greek to `l` word by word, `l` against `i`, remembered English in `i`**: no case, tense, mood or particle is mistranslated in `l`. No `i` reads as an English phrase that arrived fully formed; the one near-candidate is listed under refused.

## Open for the caller (not mine to change: it needs `t`)

1. **Units 9 and 10 (16.127–128) and check 6.** Both are word-for-word repeats of 1.250 and 1.251, which stand in odyssey-003 as two units; the second one's shipped English carries a closing ” that does not fit here. This is the case QUESTIONS.md describes under odyssey-025, item 1. The precedent fix there was to join the repeated half-line into a larger unit so the repeat rule no longer applies. Recommended: merge units 9 and 10 into one unit (t = "τοὶ δὲ φθινύθουσιν ἔδοντες\nοἶκον ἐμόν· τάχα δή με διαρραίσουσι καὶ αὐτόν.", two lines, ends at the full stop in line 128), with `l` = "and they waste away, by eating,\nmy house; soon indeed they will shatter me, myself as well." and `i` = "and meanwhile they are eating up my house and wasting it away; and before long they will be the ruin of me too.", and a note that merges the two current notes. If the units stay separate, unit 10 only passes check 6 with the stray ” (`l` …“myself as well.”” and `i` …“me too.”” as shipped), which would leave an unmatched closing mark mid-speech.
2. **Packet detection.** `packet.md` lists no repeat for 16.127 or 16.128 because it only matches whole printed lines; half-line units that coincide (and 16.137, 16.157–158 with different final punctuation) are missed. Worth fixing in `packet.py` before 079.

## Considered and refused

- **Unit 48 (184–185) contains an ano teleia after τετυγμένα· and runs on to φείδεο δ’ ἡμέων.** The rule says a unit ends at the ano teleia. But 21 of the 4,424 published units also carry an internal stop (e.g. odyssey-039 line 60, -041 line 252), the unit is two lines and closes the speech, and splitting would leave a three-word unit and require changing `t`. Left as drafted.
- **Unit 21 `l` ends with a full stop where `i` ends "?".** `l` follows Murray's stops (he prints no question mark anywhere in 137–145) and the Greek word order; the unit 20 note says so. Not an error.
- **"heaven" for οὐρανός in `i` (new row, 16.183, 200, 211).** The table's usual `i` is "sky" (5.184, 11.17), but it also has "heaven" in both layers for 11.316 and the row justifies the choice (the gods' domain). Accepted; the new row should be ratified as written.
- **αὔτως `i` "as he used to" against the table's 14.151 "without more ado".** The new row records the reason (a verb of eating and drinking, sense from the contrast with 139–141) and the note says the sense is taken from context. Accepted; the table's 14.151 row should be broadened, not the unit changed.
- **περικλυτός "very famous" against shipped 4.8 "far-famed" (odyssey-014).** The table row (8.287) governs and fixes "very famous"; 4.8 is an older divergence, as with 3.153 and 3.59. Left.
- **Unit 24 note: "This gives the reason for the grief".** A defensible reading of γάρ (it explains why they must leave Laertes alone: what they would most choose is out of reach). Left.
- **Unit 52 `i` "No, I am your father".** "No" renders ἀλλά after the negative in 187, `l` has "But father yours I am", and nothing in it is a fixed phrase from a translation. Left.
- **Unit 55 `l` "again, with words, answering him, addressed him:".** One word longer than the table's 5.96 row but exactly the shape of the shipped first-person row for 9.258 ("with words, answering him, I addressed him"). Left.
- **Unit 40 "χρυσείῃ is the Ionic form of χρυσῇ".** Epic/Ionic -ῃ for contracted -ῇ; true enough for the note's purpose. Left.
- **Unit 3 `i` "a lone line", unit 13 `i` "I myself shall stay".** Idiom choices, no sense lost. Left.
- **Unit 35 "μεγάροιο … here the main room of the hut".** Supported inside the part: he goes out from the μέγαρον (165) and back ἐς κλισίην (178). Left.
- **Unit 47 `l` "of those who hold the wide heaven" against the new row's "who hold the wide heaven".** The added "of those" renders τις θεός … τοί (one of those who); the formula words are the row's. Left.
- **Unit 7 repeats 1.245–248 with `l`/`i` identical though `t` lacks a final ν in κοιρανέουσι.** The letters-only key differs, so check 6 does not bind it, and reusing the shipped English is what the rule asks for; the note states the difference. Left.

Pass 2 (gloss.json parses against the lines) still to do.
